activity_context.topic_title: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums

examples.knowledge_point: Expressing the Limit of a Left Riemann Sum as a Definite Integral
examples.problem: Find the function $f(x)$ and the value of $b,$ given that $\displaystyle \int_{3}^b f(x)\, \textrm d x =\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left[\left(3 + \dfrac{5k}{n}\right)^2\cdot \dfrac 5 n\right].$
examples.worked_solution:
A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows:

$$
\int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm d x = \lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}f\left(x_k\right)\cdot \Delta x
$$

where $\Delta x = \dfrac{b-a}{n}$ and $x_k = a + k\Delta x.$

Notice that we're given that the lower limit $a = 3.$ 

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that $\Delta x = \dfrac{5}{n}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\dfrac{5}{n} = \dfrac{b-3}{n} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad b = 8.
$$

Consequently, $x_k = 3 + \dfrac{5k}{n}$ and $f(x_k) = x_{k}^2.$

Hence,

$$
\int_{3}^{8} x^2 \, \textrm d x =\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left[\left(3 + \dfrac{5k}{n}\right)^2\cdot \dfrac 5 n\right].
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $f(x)= x^2$ and $b = 8.$

feedback.problem: What is ${\int }_{1}^{5}\sqrt{x-1}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
feedback.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}\sqrt{x-1}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\sqrt{x-1},$ the lower bound is $a=1,$ and the upper bound is $b=5.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{5-1}{n}=\frac{4}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}\sqrt{x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(1+i\cdot \frac{4}{n})\,\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(1+\frac{4i}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\sqrt{1+\frac{4i}{n}-1}\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\sqrt{\frac{4i}{n}}\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\sqrt{\frac{i}{n}}\cdot \frac{8}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
